title: Economic Statistics
curriculum_locator: Stat H-204 Economic Statistics & Stat H-210 Lab; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Index Numbers: Foundations, Weighted Aggregates & Construction Methods
scope: Nature, purpose, and utility of economic index numbers in macroeconomic measurement
Base period selection: fixed-base vs chain-base systems, shifting and splicing of series
Simple aggregates and simple averages of price relatives: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic
Weighted aggregative price and quantity index numbers: Laspeyres, Paasche, and Fisher ideal index
Alternative formulations: Marshall-Edgeworth, Dorbish-Bowley, and Walsh geometric weighted indexes

units.title: Axiomatic Tests of Index Numbers & Cost-of-Living Metrics
scope: Irving Fisher's axiomatic criteria: Time Reversal Test, Factor Reversal Test, and Circular Test
Mathematical proof that Fisher's index satisfies Time and Factor Reversal Tests while Laspeyres and Paasche fail
The Unit Test and the non-existence of an index satisfying all axiomatic tests simultaneously (Wald's theorem)
Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Cost of Living Index Number (COLIN): Family Budget vs Aggregate Expenditure
Economic deflators, real wage calculation, purchasing power of money, and base-year rebasing

units.title: Time Series Analysis: Decomposition Models & Secular Trend Estimation
scope: Classical decomposition of economic time series: Secular trend (T), Seasonal (S), Cyclical (C), and Irregular (I)
Additive (Y = T + S + C + I) vs Multiplicative (Y = T * S * C * I) time series models and log transformation
Estimation of secular trend: Method of Semi-Averages and moving average smoothing (odd vs even centered windows)
Least squares polynomial trend fitting: linear, quadratic, exponential, and orthogonal polynomial methods
Modified exponential, Gompertz, and logistic trend curves in economic growth series

units.title: Measurement of Seasonal Variations & Cyclical Fluctuations
scope: Nature and causes of seasonal variations in economic indicators and business cycles
Simple averages method and percentage-to-trend method for seasonal indices
Ratio-to-Moving Average method (Census X-11 foundation) and seasonal adjustment (deseasonalization)
Link relative method (Karl Pearson) and adjustment for trend bias
Measurement of cyclical fluctuations: residual method, percentage of trend, and business cycle turning points

units.title: Income Distribution, Economic Inequality & Poverty Measurement
scope: Size distribution of personal income and Pareto's Law of Income Distribution: N(x) = A x^(-alpha)
Mathematical properties and estimation of the Pareto coefficient alpha from empirical income data
The Lorenz curve: continuous mathematical definition, convex curvature, and bounds
The Gini Concentration Coefficient: geometric derivation, pairwise mean difference formula, and properties
Poverty metrics: Headcount Ratio (H), Poverty Gap Index (PGI), Foster-Greer-Thorbecke (FGT) family, and Sen's index

units.title: Macroeconomic Statistics & National Income Accounting
scope: Conceptual foundations of national income: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) vs Gross National Product (GNP)
Net National Product (NNP), Gross National Income (GNI), and National Income at factor cost vs market price
The three canonical measurement approaches: Output/Production, Income, and Expenditure methods
Avoidance of double counting: value-added method, intermediate consumption vs final goods
Real vs Nominal GDP, GDP Deflator, and international comparisons via Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)

units.title: Input-Output Analysis & Social Accounting Systems
scope: Wassily Leontief's open static Input-Output model and inter-industry flow matrices
Technical input coefficients a_ij = x_ij / X_j and technology matrix A
The Leontief balance equations (I - A) X = F and the Leontief inverse (I - A)^(-1)
Hawkins-Simon conditions for the economic viability of input-output systems
Direct and indirect backward and forward linkage multipliers and Social Accounting Matrix (SAM) structure

units.title: Statistical Demand, Supply & Econometric Elasticity Analysis
scope: Microeconomic demand theory and mathematical formulation of Marshallian demand functions
Price elasticity of demand (point and arc elasticity), income elasticity, and cross-price elasticity
Engel curves: mathematical formulations for necessities, luxuries, and inferior goods (linear, semi-log, double-log)
Statistical estimation of market demand curves: log-log regression models and identification problems
Supply curve elasticity and equilibrium price determination under empirical shifts
